description:
Found by the fz-sc8.165 builder; measured on 6f631de13.
`:z < :a` (two static atoms) allocates 2 scalar boxes on run and build and 0 on interp (Process.heap_alloc_stats scalar_box_allocs delta around the expression). They are ints: the result of compare and the literal 0.
Mechanism as read from the backend dump (not independently re-derived): Kernel.</2 has the generic clause `def left < right, do: compare(left, right) < 0`, which calls </2 again with int arguments. The spec for (atom, atom) therefore has parameters typed `int | :z` and `int | :a` (key Kernel.</2[atom, atom], param_reprs [ValueRef, ValueRef]), and the tail call boxes the two raw ints into those ValueRef lanes (emit_tail_call_term -> push_binding_as_abi_arg, RawInt to ValueRef). The same shape with a typed `c < 0` allocates nothing.
Also unexplained and possibly the same cause: send(self(), :ping) followed by a receive allocates 1 scalar box on run and build and 0 on interp; it is not an atom.
Done when: both expressions allocate 0 scalar boxes on interp, run and build, pinned by a behavior fixture; the cause is fixed where the spec join widens the recursive call, not by a special case for </2.
title: Comparing two atoms with < boxes no integers in native code
